subject: Where customer data lives and stepwise erasure playbook
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@crestline.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Data Privacy Team <privacy@crestline.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Quick Q — where does our data live & how do we get things deleted?

Jordan —

Thanks for the demo earlier. Crestline's legal/privacy folks raised a couple of practical questions we need answered before the pilot:

1) By default, where do user requests (raw prompts) and generated outputs live (region / storage class)?
2) If a customer asks to remove a handful of chat sessions (example attached redacted.csv with timestamps), what are the exact steps and expected timeline?
3) Are there differences between streaming fragments (partial tokens) and final outputs when it comes to deletion?
4) For requests that include PII, do you have an expedited path or proof-of-deletion evidence we can share with auditors?

Attached: crestline-security-questions-v2.pdf and a tiny redacted sample.

Appreciate short concrete steps we can put in our procurement checklist.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, Crestline Systems
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@crestline.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q — where does our data live & how do we get things deleted?

Samir — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise playbook (kept short so you can paste into procurement). If you want a formal PDF I can have ops generate one.

Summary (short answers):
- Default residency: US regions (multi-AZ) unless customer requests EU-only; residency is set at account creation.
- What we store by default:
  * Requests / prompts: retained in ephemeral logs for 30 days by default and then removed from active stores (short-lived caches may remain for up to 72 hours for debugging).
  * Streaming fragments (token buffers): ephemeral, flushed within 7 days by default; we do not index fragments for search.
  * Final model outputs (responses/completions) and derived artefacts: stored in the customer log store for 180 days by default (used for billing, debugging, and quality regressions) unless the customer enables a shorter TTL.
  * Audit/log metadata (request id, timestamps, server-side tracing info): retained for 1 year for operational troubleshooting; larger compliance exports are retained per contract.

Stepwise erasure process (how Crestline requests deletion and what to expect):
1) Create a Data Erasure Request (DER) via our support portal and include: account id, timeframe, list of example request ids or timestamps (redacted.csv you attached works). Link: https://support.redwood.ai/requests/DER-8392
2) We acknowledge within 24 business hours and validate scope with you if needed.
3) Engineering runs a scoped purge job across the account's regional stores. The purge kicks off within 72 hours of validation.
4) Purge mechanics: requests and streaming fragments are removed from active stores immediately; dependent cached artifacts (prefix/KV cache) are invalidated; backups and cold-archival indexes are scheduled for deletion per the regional retention policy (see notes on backups below).
5) Confirmation & evidence: we provide a deletion report listing the object keys and purge timestamps within 30 days of job completion. If you require certified proof of deletion (hashes + log snapshots), add that to the DER and legal will create a tailored certificate (this may be tied to an SOW).

Items that commonly confuse customers:
- If your app opted into "store_requests" or enabled S3 exports, those external exports must be deleted from the external destination separately — Redwood only removes data we host.
- Audit logs and billing records are treated separately; we can discuss varying retention for compliance needs during contracting.

Attachments: I pulled your redacted sample and flagged the example request ids to make the purge precise.

If that looks good I can loop in Ops to schedule a trial purge on a narrow time window.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions (Redwood Inference)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@crestline.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q — where does our data live & how do we get things deleted?

Samir / Jordan — quick legal addendum so Crestline has what auditors expect:

- Evidence: our standard deletion report includes object ids, timestamps, the region where purge occurred, and the engineer-run job id. For higher-assurance requests we can add signed statements and an export of the system audit trail showing the purge transaction.
- Backups & retention: short-term backups used for disaster recovery are included in the purge cycle; long-term archival snapshots (if present per contract) require an explicit archival-wipe instruction in the DER.
- SLA for regulated erasure: we offer a 30-day cert turnaround for enterprise contracts (this is separate from the default 30-day confirmation window Jordan mentioned and should be added to the contract if required).

If you want, Jordan, I can draft a one-paragraph clause Crestline can include in procurement language that calls out: residency selection at account creation, default TTLs (prompts 30d / fragments 7d / outputs 180d), and DER mechanics.

—Kimberly Park
Legal Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@crestline.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 06 Nov 2026 14:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q — where does our data live & how do we get things deleted?

Thanks Jordan and Kimberly — that's exactly the level of detail we needed. Two quick follow-ups:

1) We'll file the DER later today with the sample rows and ask for the certification option.
2) Can you confirm EU-only residency is available for pilot accounts (we may spin a EU pilot later)? If yes, we will include the residency switch in the DER.

We'll proceed and keep you posted.

Samir
Head of Product, Crestline Systems
